paragraphs: An agent completing a long workflow may need to repeat operations, branch on results, combine information, and retry failed calls. Static web endpoints expose individual operations, but they express these larger workflows poorly. ToolPro addresses this mismatch by turning the agent’s intended interaction into an executable program that describes multiple service operations together.

The program includes explicit information about effects, allowing the system to distinguish operations that modify state. ToolPro combines construction guided by constraints with replay that accounts for these effects, supporting exactly-once execution of state-changing calls. It also uses execution profiles to decide when running a program is preferable to making calls individually, making the choice responsive to the workflow.

The researchers implement ToolPro over MCP-style services using WebAssembly sandboxing. Across workflows involving real applications, they report latency reductions of up to 53.4% and client-side traffic reductions of up to 96.1%. Gains grow with network latency and workflow complexity, indicating where this richer interface offers particular value.
icml-2026-beyond-static-endpoints-tool-p.tldr: ToolPro packages multi-step service interactions into executable programs, reducing latency and client traffic in evaluated agent workflows.

paragraphs: Finding a clip that matches a description is only part of assembling a coherent video. A continuation also needs to respect the visual state and identities established by earlier clips. This paper formalizes Consistent Video Retrieval to study that requirement and introduces a diagnostic benchmark spanning YouCook2, COIN, and CrossTask.

CAST is a lightweight adapter that adds context awareness to frozen vision-language representations. It uses visual history to predict a residual update: a change to the representation conditioned on the current state. This gives retrieval an explicit way to account for how a scene evolves, while allowing the adapter to work with different underlying embedding models.

Experiments show improvements on YouCook2 and CrossTask, competitive results on COIN, and consistent gains over zero-shot baselines across multiple foundation backbones. CAST also supplies a useful signal for reranking video continuations generated by black-box systems. These findings support using visual history both to retrieve compatible clips and to select more coherent generated continuations.
icml-2026-cast-modeling-visual-state-tra.tldr: CAST uses visual history to improve clip retrieval and rerank generated continuations for greater temporal consistency.

paragraphs: Routing chooses which model in a pool should handle a query. Supervised routers need costly preference labels and can struggle when incoming queries change. Reasoning models add another complication: their output contains a thinking process followed by an answer, and the much longer thinking portion can overwhelm the answer when assessing the output.

ReasoningRouter addresses both the unequal lengths and the relationship between these components. It balances their contributions when constructing embeddings, then uses a probabilistic model to represent the dependency from thinking to answer. Its proposed Causal Triangulation Property enables estimation of the quality of each component and their causal connection without requiring labels.

The paper reports competitive routing accuracy together with computational efficiency. A further contribution is the ability to assess reasoning quality and answer quality separately, providing a more differentiated account of model behavior. This matters because a routing decision can then draw on the structure of a reasoning model’s output instead of treating the entire response as one undivided signal.
icml-2026-causal-dependency-aware-unsupe.tldr: ReasoningRouter routes without labels by balancing reasoning and answer representations and modeling their dependency.

paragraphs: Safety training often alternates between finding attacks against a fixed model and repairing the vulnerabilities those attacks expose. That separation can leave attackers practicing outdated exploits while defenders respond to threats discovered earlier. Self-RedTeam instead trains attacking and defending behavior together, so each side continually encounters an evolving opponent.

A single policy plays both roles: it creates adversarial prompts and produces responses to them. A reward model judges the outcomes, and each role uses private reasoning for strategic planning. The method frames this interaction as a two-player zero-sum game. Its theoretical guarantee is conditional: if the game reaches a Nash equilibrium, the defender gives safe responses against any adversarial input within that formulation.

Experiments cover five Llama and Qwen models and 14 benchmarks. The paper reports a 17.80% increase in attack diversity measured with SBERT and safety improvements of up to 95% for RLHF-trained models. These results support ongoing co-adaptation as a practical safety-training approach, while the equilibrium condition remains essential to the theoretical claim.
icml-2026-chasing-moving-targets-with-on.tldr: Self-RedTeam jointly evolves attacking and defending behavior through online self-play, with empirical safety gains and an equilibrium-conditional guarantee.

paragraphs: Supervised fine-tuning teaches a language model to imitate expert examples, often before reinforcement learning begins. With a small expert dataset, this adaptation can weaken broader abilities. The paper identifies tokens that the base model considers unlikely as the main source of this degradation in its analysis: they differ strongly from the model’s existing knowledge and produce larger training gradients.

The researchers study token-wise clipping, which bounds updates associated with individual tokens. Limiting the influence of low-probability tokens changes what the model prioritizes during learning. Adaptation becomes more gradual, allowing it to fit expert data while better preserving general capabilities that can support exploration during later reinforcement learning.

Compared with standard supervised fine-tuning, clipping reduces out-of-distribution forgetting by 11.54% and improves final reinforcement-learning performance by 7.09% across the agentic benchmarks. Analysis of internal representations also finds smaller changes under clipping. Together, these findings connect control over individual training updates with a more generalizable starting point for the next training stage.
icml-2026-clipping-low-probability-token.tldr: Bounding updates from unlikely expert tokens helps supervised fine-tuning preserve general abilities and improves subsequent reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: A graphical-interface agent must identify where to interact on a screen. As new interface domains and screen resolutions arrive, the locations and sizes of relevant elements change. The paper introduces Continual GUI Agents as a task in which agents keep learning under these shifts, and finds that existing methods struggle to maintain reliable grounding over time.

GUI-Anchoring in Flux, or GUI-AiF, addresses this problem through reinforcement fine-tuning. It introduces one reward for interaction points and another for interaction regions. Together, these rewards guide the agent to follow changing targets and areas, reducing the tendency to become overly dependent on fixed coordinates or element scales learned from static interfaces.

The reported experiments show GUI-AiF outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. The contribution is both a continual-learning formulation for interface agents and a reward design tailored to the way interfaces change. The results suggest that reinforcement fine-tuning can help preserve useful grounding as an agent encounters successive changes in its visual interaction environment.
icml-2026-continual-gui-agents-6e53aecb8.tldr: GUI-AiF uses rewards for changing interaction points and regions to improve continual learning as interfaces and resolutions shift.

paragraphs: Home health management presents a different data problem from care supported by hospital equipment. Information collected at home varies across devices and situations, while an individual’s needs and conditions can change. DIYHealth Suite addresses these challenges through a coordinated dataset, model, and evaluation benchmark designed around home care.

DIYHealth-900K brings together multimodal data covering diverse real-world home-care scenarios. DIYHealthGPT builds on this resource as an adaptive foundation model, using a technique called Hybrid Hyper Low-Rank Adaptation to support adaptation. DIYHealthBench supplies a shared evaluation framework for the broad range of tasks involved, addressing the lack of a unified basis for comparing models in this setting.

Experiments evaluate 11 home-care tasks in both open-question and closed-question settings. The paper reports state-of-the-art performance over general-purpose and medical-specific baselines. These findings establish a stronger evaluated approach to home-care questions and tasks, while the suite’s broader contribution is to connect representative data, an adaptive model, and systematic assessment for personalized health management.
icml-2026-diyhealth-suite-dataset-model-.tldr: DIYHealth Suite combines home-care data, an adaptive model, and a benchmark, reporting leading performance on 11 home-care tasks.

paragraphs: Knowledge distillation transfers information between models, but different tokenizers can make their predictions difficult to align. When their vocabularies overlap little, noisy correspondences can make distillation perform worse than ordinary supervised fine-tuning. The paper identifies this as a low-overlap negative-transfer regime and develops E-SCOT to address it.

E-SCOT treats alignment as a sparse transport problem using a comparison measure that does not depend on shared vocabulary. It anchors lexical matches to text spans, restricting which correspondences are considered and preserving locality. Constructing this support set takes time linear in sequence length, avoiding the dense sequence-level matching used by earlier transport approaches. An entropy-based weighting mechanism then directs more distillation effort toward informative positions with substantial differences in uncertainty profiles.

Across experiments involving diverse model families, the authors report state-of-the-art performance and elimination of negative transfer in the tested low-overlap settings. The findings show why both correspondence quality and selective allocation of the learning signal matter when transferring knowledge across incompatible tokenizations.
icml-2026-entropy-aware-span-constrained.tldr: E-SCOT combines sparse span alignment with uncertainty-based weighting to improve distillation between models with different tokenizers.

paragraphs: Designing one molecule to interact with multiple biological targets requires satisfying several binding constraints together. Methods that represent each protein pocket independently can struggle to capture what a shared ligand needs across different sites. This paper proposes a generative framework centered on pocket structure to support that joint design problem.

The protein representation filters out residues considered irrelevant to the ligand while retaining information about backbone folding and spatial proximity between residues inside binding pockets. This focuses the representation on the geometry involved in binding. The framework also combines structural information with amino acid and nucleotide sequences, bringing complementary information into the representation across targets.

Experiments involving COVID-19, schizophrenia, and tumor targets produce valid molecular candidates with significantly improved binding affinities relative to state-of-the-art methods. The stated result concerns candidate generation and binding affinity. Its methodological significance is that the design process can account for multiple heterogeneous pockets together, using both their local geometry and associated sequence information to guide a single shared molecule.
icml-2026-geometric-pocket-centric-prote.tldr: A pocket-centered generative framework combines binding-site geometry and sequence information to improve multi-target molecular candidate design.

paragraphs: Domain generalization asks a model to remain predictive in a target environment it never sees during training. Simply matching representations across training domains can damage the structure that distinguishes classes, especially with finite data. RDI addresses this by controlling the geometry of each class’s representation as well as its alignment across domains.

The framework represents each class using a low-dimensional subspace and extends rate–distortion ideas to the space of these subspaces, called a Grassmann manifold. One objective brings corresponding subspaces into alignment across domains. A second controls their spectral and volumetric complexity. The two terms aim to make alignment stable while preserving the geometric distinctions needed for prediction.

The paper provides finite-sample stability guarantees under bounded distribution shifts. On DomainBed, RDI performs competitively with strong domain-generalization baselines. Ablation results support the need for both alignment and complexity control in the evaluated approach. The contribution is therefore a principled way to balance cross-domain agreement with retention of class-discriminative structure.
icml-2026-geometric-ratedistortion-invar.tldr: RDI aligns class-specific subspaces across domains while controlling complexity to preserve predictive geometry under distribution shifts.

paragraphs: Optimization becomes expensive when keeping each update inside a complicated constraint set requires a difficult projection. Hom-PGD+ studies non-convex sets that are homeomorphic to a ball: their geometry permits a continuous, reversible correspondence with a ball. This class includes star-shaped sets encountered in machine learning and engineering.

The method trains an invertible neural network to learn that correspondence. It then expresses the optimization problem in ball coordinates, where projecting an update back into the allowed region is efficient. This reparameterization replaces expensive projection or optimization oracles with computations through the learned network, with per-iteration complexity linear in its number of parameters.

The convergence rate is O(ε⁻²) to an approximately stationary solution, with accuracy ε plus a term proportional to the square root of the mapping’s learning error. Thus mapping quality directly affects the guarantee. Experiments on quadratically constrained quadratic programs, chance-constrained power systems, and non-uniform adversarial attacks report competitive solution quality and speedups of up to an order of magnitude.
icml-2026-hom-pgd-fast-reparameterized-o.tldr: Hom-PGD+ learns an invertible mapping to a ball to make constrained optimization faster, with accuracy depending on mapping error.

paragraphs: A membership inference attack estimates whether a particular data point appeared in a model’s training set. Strong existing attacks often train many reference models to characterize the score distribution associated with each point. That repeated training makes the attack computationally costly. Bayesian Membership Inference Attack, or BMIA, seeks to obtain this information more efficiently.

BMIA applies a Laplace approximation to one reference model, constructing an approximate posterior distribution over its parameters. Sampling from that distribution enables direct estimation of the conditional score distribution used by the attack. The paper’s theoretical analysis shows that Bayesian sampling reduces intra-model variance, connecting this statistical effect to stronger attack performance.

The same reasoning motivates a version that uses several reference models when they are available, further improving performance. Experiments across image, text, and tabular data report state-of-the-art effectiveness and efficiency. The contribution links a computational shortcut to a statistical explanation: parameter sampling can provide useful attack information without relying solely on separately training a large collection of reference models.
icml-2026-how-does-bayesian-sampling-hel.tldr: BMIA uses Bayesian parameter sampling to estimate membership-attack score distributions more efficiently and improve attack effectiveness.

paragraphs: Scene graphs describe objects and the relationships between them, connecting image understanding to structured reasoning. Training-free approaches based on vision-language models reduce the need for scarce annotations, but can invent relationships and flatten part–whole structure. HSGG addresses both problems through a hierarchy of entities followed by geometry-guided relation inference.

The first stage combines top-down expansion of objects with bottom-up reasoning about attributes to build multiple levels of scene structure. The second stage filters out spatially implausible object pairs using image-plane proximity, depth information, and object scale. It then contrasts predictions from a visually grounded expert with a hallucination-prone geometric prior to suppress unsupported relation labels.

Experiments show generalization to previously unseen objects and predicates without training, substantial reductions in relational hallucinations, and consistent improvements in downstream reasoning. The approach matters because it uses hierarchy to organize what is present and geometry to constrain what relationships are plausible. Together, these components improve the structured information available to later reasoning tasks.
icml-2026-hsgg-training-free-hierarchica.tldr: HSGG builds hierarchical scene graphs without training and uses geometric constraints to reduce hallucinated relationships.

paragraphs: Model-size scaling laws summarize how prediction loss changes as language models grow, but depth and width need not contribute in the same way. This paper isolates depth by examining language models and simplified residual networks. It finds a regime in which loss decreases in inverse proportion to the number of layers.

The authors propose that this pattern probably comes from many layers performing similar functions. Their contributions may reduce error through an averaging effect, rather than through a sequence of increasingly composed computations or the discretization of smooth dynamics. This interpretation makes the observed scaling informative about how additional layers are being used, beyond simply showing that deeper models perform better.

The paper describes this regime as robust but inefficient. It suggests that residual-network architectural biases and target functions incompatible with smooth dynamics may help produce it. The resulting design implication is qualified: making language models more efficient may require architectures that encourage layers to build more compositionally on one another.
icml-2026-inverse-depth-scaling-from-mos.tldr: The paper finds inverse-depth loss scaling and proposes that similar layers may improve predictions through averaging rather than compositional computation.

paragraphs: Robotic vision-language-action models learn to turn observations and instructions into actions, but real robot action data are scarce. Latent action models offer extra supervision by learning visual changes from unlabeled human videos. When these two models are trained separately, however, the latent representations stay fixed and cannot be corrected by the robot’s action-learning process.

LARA jointly optimizes the two models by aligning their representations. Action trajectories help the latent action model distinguish meaningful action-related changes from distracting visual changes. In the other direction, its learned forward dynamics constrain the action model, reducing its tendency to generate trajectories that appear plausible but fail to accomplish useful physical effects.

The authors evaluate LARA for pretraining, enhancing pretrained action models, and refining latent action models. Across three simulation benchmarks and one real-world manipulation benchmark, they report average improvements of 10%, 5%, and 15% for these uses, respectively. The results support the value of reciprocal learning: each model supplies information that addresses a weakness in the other.
icml-2026-lara-latent-action-representat.tldr: LARA jointly aligns latent action and vision-language-action models so visual dynamics and robot trajectories improve each other.

paragraphs: Robots need to reason about physical situations while producing actions quickly enough for manipulation. Explicit reasoning traces add inference delay, and language can struggle to express fine physical details. LaST₀ addresses these problems by reasoning in a compact latent space that represents information relevant to robotic control.

Its latent reasoning includes future visual dynamics, three-dimensional structure, and the robot’s own state. Extending these representations through time supports consistent implicit reasoning trajectories. A Mixture-of-Transformers architecture separates a reasoning expert, which operates less frequently, from an acting expert that generates frequent actions conditioned on the latent representations. Training with different operation frequencies supports adaptive switching during deployment.

The evaluation covers 10 real-world tasks involving tabletop manipulation, mobile manipulation, and dexterous hands. The paper reports mean success-rate improvements of 13%, 14%, and 14% over prior state-of-the-art vision-language-action methods in these categories, respectively. These findings support separating the frequency of physical reasoning from the frequency of action generation while keeping the two coordinated.
icml-2026-last-0-latent-spatio-temporal-.tldr: LaST₀ combines slower latent physical reasoning with faster action generation to improve real-world robotic manipulation.

paragraphs: Estimating a treatment’s causal effect requires choosing adjustment variables carefully. Existing selection methods often require a complete causal structure, exclude unobserved variables, or restrict candidate variables to those unaffected by the treatment or outcome. These requirements can be difficult to satisfy, and learning the whole causal structure can be computationally expensive.

The paper first characterizes, using local causal structure, the boundary between cases where an adjustment set exists and cases where it does not. It then develops a local learning method for choosing covariates in nonparametric causal effect estimation. The method accommodates latent variables and does not require the stated pretreatment restriction on candidate covariates.

The authors prove soundness and completeness under standard assumptions, so the theoretical claim remains conditional on those assumptions. Experiments on synthetic and real-world data support the method’s effectiveness. Its contribution is to make local information sufficient for the proposed selection procedure, reducing dependence on global structure learning while allowing a broader range of causal settings.
icml-2026-local-covariate-selection-for-.tldr: A local covariate-selection method supports causal effect estimation with latent variables and without requiring the pretreatment assumption.

paragraphs: A robot learning new skills over time can lose competence on tasks it previously mastered. Much earlier work examined this problem in small policies trained from scratch. This paper studies large pretrained vision-language-action models and finds that their continual-learning behavior differs substantially: they are more resistant to forgetting than the smaller policies considered.

Simple experience replay, which revisits stored examples from earlier tasks, works particularly well with these pretrained models. In some cases, even a small replay dataset yields zero forgetting. The analysis identifies pretraining as a critical factor, allowing models to retain earlier capabilities with a small buffer while still learning new tasks effectively.

The researchers also distinguish reduced task performance from complete loss of relevant knowledge. Models can preserve information about earlier tasks even when their visible performance declines, enabling rapid recovery through fine-tuning. These findings suggest that large-scale pretraining changes both how forgetting appears and how much machinery is needed to manage it, making simple replay effective in the studied settings.
icml-2026-pretrained-vision-language-act.tldr: Pretrained vision-language-action models show strong resistance to forgetting, with simple replay sometimes preserving all measured prior performance.

paragraphs: Code-generation training can draw from collections containing several verified correct implementations for each problem. Choosing which solutions to include introduces another design decision. This paper tests whether sophisticated selection methods, such as prioritizing diversity or difficulty, improve on randomly choosing solutions within each problem’s verified pool.

The comparison spans multiple base language models and selection methods based on continuous embeddings, token sequences, and syntactic structure. Random sampling remains consistently competitive across the models and shows greater stability across models than the more complex strategies. The result challenges the expectation that additional selection machinery will reliably produce better training data in this setting.

The authors interpret this through implicit knowledge consensus: verified solution pools may already contain representative algorithmic patterns that random selection preserves. This is a proposed explanation for the empirical finding. Their practical recommendation is to use random sampling as an inexpensive default, turning to specialized selectors when the objective specifically requires coverage of difficult cases or particular constraints.
icml-2026-random-selection-reveals-impli.tldr: Randomly selecting verified code solutions is consistently competitive and more stable across models than the complex selectors studied.

paragraphs: General-purpose robot models face limited training data and difficulty transferring skills between hardware platforms. RDT2 addresses these problems with a robotic foundation model built on a seven-billion-parameter vision-language model. Its goal is zero-shot deployment on previously unseen robot embodiments while handling tasks expressed through open-vocabulary instructions.

The project combines model design with more than 10,000 hours of demonstrations collected using an enhanced Universal Manipulation Interface designed to be independent of embodiment. A three-stage training process connects discrete linguistic knowledge to continuous control through residual vector quantization, flow matching, and distillation. Distillation also supports the model’s real-time inference requirements.

The paper reports zero-shot generalization to unseen objects, scenes, instructions, and robotic platforms. It also reports outperforming state-of-the-art baselines on dexterous, long-horizon, and dynamic tasks, including table tennis. The contribution brings together broad demonstration collection and a training pipeline for translating language-oriented representations into control, addressing both the data and execution demands of transfer across robot bodies.
icml-2026-rdt2-exploring-the-scaling-lim.tldr: RDT2 combines large-scale embodiment-independent demonstrations with staged training to support zero-shot transfer across robotic platforms and tasks.

paragraphs: In decentralized learning, different nodes can contribute unequally to the global objective. One strategy incorporates these weights into local losses and uses a doubly stochastic communication matrix. Another preserves the original losses and encodes the weights in a row-stochastic matrix. Both target the same weighted objective, but their convergence behavior can differ.

The paper analyzes these strategies in a weighted Hilbert space that reflects the node weights, obtaining tighter convergence rates than standard Euclidean analysis. In this geometry, the row-stochastic design is self-adjoint. The doubly stochastic design lacks that property, introducing additional penalty terms that amplify disagreement between nodes. This exposes a source of slowdown beyond the familiar spectral-gap comparison.

The authors derive sufficient conditions for the row-stochastic approach to converge faster even when its spectral gap is smaller. They also obtain network-topology conditions guaranteeing this advantage through eigenvalue comparisons. The result does not establish universal superiority; it identifies circumstances where matching communication to the weighted objective yields a provable benefit and informs topology design.
icml-2026-row-stochastic-matrices-can-pr.tldr: Weighted-space analysis identifies conditions where row-stochastic communication converges faster than doubly stochastic designs, even with a smaller spectral gap.

paragraphs: Prediction intervals are useful only when their coverage remains reliable for the conditions under which predictions are made. Kernel-based conditional conformal methods address complex changes in input distributions, but their computational expense can limit practical use. SpeedCP builds on an existing regularized kernel framework to make this form of calibration more efficient.

Its central algorithm computes the full optimization solution path at essentially the cost of a single kernel quantile fit. It also tunes hyperparameters simultaneously, supporting control over smoothness and calibration that adapts to the data. For high-dimensional inputs, the method incorporates low-rank latent embeddings, with conditional validity captured in that learned representation space.

Across evaluations with modern black-box predictors, SpeedCP provides reliable conditional coverage. Relative to the framework it builds on, the paper reports a 30% improvement in interval length and a 40-fold speedup. These findings connect computational savings with more informative uncertainty intervals, while the latent-space extension provides a way to apply the approach in higher-dimensional settings.
icml-2026-speedcp-fast-kernel-based-cond.tldr: SpeedCP accelerates kernel-based conditional conformal calibration while reporting reliable coverage and improved prediction-interval length.

paragraphs: Fine-tuning on harmful material can undo a language model’s safety alignment. This paper investigates that process through attention sinks, using a statistic called sink divergence for each attention head. The researchers observe heads with positive and negative divergence, and find that the number with positive divergence grows as harmfulness increases during harmful fine-tuning.

From this association, they propose the separable sink divergence hypothesis: heads involved in learning harmful patterns can be distinguished by the sign of this statistic. Surgery turns that hypothesis into a defense applied during fine-tuning. A regularizer suppresses sink divergence, steering heads toward the negative-divergence group and reducing the tendency to learn and amplify harmful patterns.

Experiments report defense-performance improvements of 5.90% on BeaverTails, 11.25% on HarmBench, and 9.55% on SorryBench. The contribution connects an observed internal attention signal to a training intervention with measured benefits. The separation of harmful-pattern learning by divergence sign remains the proposed hypothesis motivating the method.
icml-2026-surgery-mitigating-harmful-fin.tldr: Surgery regularizes an attention-head statistic associated with harmful learning to improve defenses against harmful fine-tuning.

paragraphs: Convergent cross mapping investigates causal relationships in time series by reconstructing representations of a system’s state from delayed observations. With noisy measurements of a single variable, those reconstructions can have distorted geometry. Points that appear nearby may then provide unreliable information, weakening the causal conclusions drawn from cross mapping.

TopoDistill improves these single-variable reconstructions using information from multiple observed variables. A global embedder learns a representation of the system’s attractor from multivariate observations. A delay embedder then learns to reproduce its neighborhood distributions. This transfers information about the system’s broader organization into the local neighborhoods used by the single-variable representation.

The paper reports that this alignment produces smoother, more reliable neighborhoods and improves cross mapping under noise while retaining specificity against spurious correlations. Theoretical analysis and experiments support its effectiveness for causal discovery. The central contribution is to improve the geometry on which causal inference relies, using a multivariate view to guide a reconstruction that would otherwise depend on one noisy view.
icml-2026-topodistill-distilling-global-.tldr: TopoDistill transfers multivariate neighborhood structure into single-variable time-series embeddings to improve causal discovery under noise.

paragraphs: Graphs can carry multiple kinds of information, but combining those modalities requires more than aggregating their representations. This paper identifies two weaknesses in existing multimodal graph foundation models: insufficient modeling of interactions between modalities and imperfect alignment between their semantic spaces. PLANET addresses these as separate problems at different representation levels.

At the embedding level, Embedding-wise Domain Gating adaptively introduces context from other modalities while accounting for graph topology. This enriches local meaning through cross-modal interaction. At the node level, Node-wise Discretization Retrieval constructs a shared discretized semantic representation space to bridge modality gaps. The division gives interaction and alignment distinct mechanisms rather than asking one operation to accomplish both.

Experiments report significant improvements over state-of-the-art baselines across graph-centered tasks and multimodal generation tasks. These findings support the framework’s strategy of separating local semantic enrichment from global alignment. The contribution is a way to combine graph structure and heterogeneous information while explicitly addressing both how modalities inform one another and how their meanings become comparable.
icml-2026-toward-effective-multimodal-gr.tldr: PLANET separates cross-modal interaction from semantic alignment to improve multimodal graph understanding and generation.
